title: Differential kernel detection
statement: Let $p$ be prime, $K$ a field of characteristic $p$, $K^p=\{x^p:x\in K\}$, and $(K_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ a family of subfields of $K$ such that $K^p\subseteq K_\alpha$ for every $\alpha$, $\bigcap_\alpha K_\alpha=K^p$, and for every $\alpha,\beta$ some $\gamma$ satisfies $K_\gamma\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_\beta$. The index set may be empty. Then an element $\omega\in\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] which maps to zero in $\Omega_{K/K_\alpha}$ for every $\alpha$ is zero, where each map sends $\mathrm da$ to $\mathrm da$.

proof.text: If the index type is empty, the intersection condition makes every element of K a p-th power. The p-th power derivation rule in characteristic p makes every absolute differential da zero. Since these generate the differential module, the entire module is zero.

For a nonempty downward directed family of intermediate fields over a base field k with infimum k, every finite k-linearly independent family in K remains independent over some field of the family. Otherwise its K-linear relation subspace contains a nonzero vector over every field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-intersection-subfields-subspace] to obtain a nonzero relation over k, contradicting independence. Enumerate any finite index type by Fin n; the empty finite family is independent over an arbitrary field of the nonempty family. Apply this observation over B = F_p K^p, extending the scalars of the given K_alpha; the hypotheses identify B with their infimum.

Choose a p-basis and its monomial basis by [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-exists], and the associated differential basis by [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-differentials-basis]. For omega take the finite support T of its differential-basis coordinates. Bounded monomials on T form a finite family: inject their exponents into T -> Fin p. Extend exponents by zero to the full p-basis index type; this embeds these monomials into the monomial basis, so they are B-independent. Step 2 gives an alpha over which they remain independent. Since K_alpha contains every p-th power, K_alpha K^p = K_alpha; scalar restriction to the bottom intermediate field gives the precise p-independence hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-p-independent-differentials-independent] to obtain independent relative differentials on T. Map the finite coordinate expansion of omega to the relative differential module using K-linearity and map_D. Its image is zero by hypothesis, so every coordinate on T is zero. Coordinates outside T are zero by definition of support; injectivity of the basis representation gives omega = 0.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07P4, proof of (1); contrapositive finite-relation formulation of Tag 07P3, with the empty-index case handled by the p-th power derivation rule.

lean.statement: theorem intersection_subfields_differentials_kernel (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (K : Type u) [Field K] [CharP K p] {ι : Type v} (Kα : ι → IntermediateField (ZMod p) K) (h₁ : ∀ α : ι, Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p) ⊆ (Kα α : Set K)) (h₂ : Set.range (fun x : K => x ^ p) = ((⨅ α, Kα α : IntermediateField (ZMod p) K) : Set K)) (h₃ : ∀ α β : ι, ∃ γ : ι, Kα γ ≤ Kα α ⊓ Kα β) : ∀ ω : Ω[K⁄ZMod p], (∀ α : ι, KaehlerDifferential.map (ZMod p) (Kα α) K K ω = 0) → ω = 0

mathlib_searches.query: Downward directed intermediate fields with Frobenius image as infimum detect zero Kahler differentials and preserve that infimum after finite field extension
In prime characteristic the intersection of a downward directed family of fields containing all pth powers detects Kahler differentials and commutes with finite extensions after adjoining pth powers
